title: Super-STORM: Molecular Modeling to Achieve Single-molecule Localization with STORM Microscopy
protocol: Coat the coverslip of the microfluidic device with human P-selectin-Fc at a concentration of 2 μg/mL and human ICAM-1-Fc at a concentration of 10 μg/mL for 2 hours at 22-24°C.
Dilute nanodiamonds (fiducial markers) in the coating solution at a ratio of 1:500 from their original concentration.
Add dilution of nanodiamonds to the coverslip along with human P-selectin-Fc and ICAM-1-Fc for coating.
Block the coated surface with 1% casein for 30 minutes at 22-24°C.
Wash the coated surface twice with PBS.
Assemble the flow chamber under buffer to avoid air interfaces.
Isolate cells from culture, blood, or tissue.
Wash isolated human neutrophils with PBS without Ca2+ and Mg2+ twice.
Resuspend the cells in RPMI-1640 without phenol red plus 2% HSA.
Add cell surface label by membrane dyes or fluorescently labeled antibody/F(ab) to an abundant GPI-anchored cell surface antigen, such as CD16 on neutrophils.
Stain cells with AF488-anti-CD16 antibody (1 μg/mL) for 10 min at 22-24°C.
Wash stained cells twice with PBS.
Resuspend the labeled cells in RPMI-1640 without phenol red plus 2% HSA.
Wash with PBS without Ca2+ and Mg2+ twice after staining.
Resuspend cells in RPMI-1640 without phenol red plus 2% HSA.
Incubate cells (5 × 10^6 mL^-1) with KIM127 and mAb24 F(ab) fragments (5 μg mL^-1 each) at 22-24°C for 3 min.
Perfuse the mixture into the microfluidic chamber without separating F(ab) fragments.
Label molecules of interest before fixation to prevent epitope loss due to fixation.
Add cells (5 × 10^6 ml^-1) to the reservoir of the microfluidic device.
Apply pressure to start the flow.
Add activator to neutrophils (e.g., IL-8 at 10 ng/mL).
Perfuse for 12 seconds.
Add fixation buffer to the reservoir, mixing to achieve a final concentration of 8% in the system.
Keep perfusing while observing cells using a bright-field microscope.
Wash for 5 minutes with the same buffer used to suspend the cells, ensuring no air bubbles are present.
Disassemble the microfluidic device.
Glue the coverslip into the hole of the Petri dish with Super Glue (Gorilla) to prevent leakage or movement.
Fill the Petri dish with 2 mL of PBS.
Transfer the sample to the microscope equipped with a 100x 1.49 NA Plan Apo TIRF oil objective.
Replace PBS with 2 mL freshly made STORM buffer in the Petri dish.
Acquire one TIRF image at each wavelength using low laser power and a 200 ms exposure time.
Capture an optional TIRF image to distinguish different cell subtypes.
Acquire raw images from the same field of view using high laser power and a short exposure time.
Capture typically 20,000 frames per channel for each fluorochrome-labeled molecule.
Adjust laser power to enable between 100 and 300 blinks per frame in the center of the field.
Test different numbers of acquisition frames to determine optimal image quality.
Apply automatic drifting correction using fiducial markers during data analysis.
Determine the localization of molecules using 2D Gaussian fitting implemented in Nikon software.
Generate and store data sheets of all STORM localizations.
Register the TIRF image with the STORM positions using fiducial markers.
Generate a STORM image using ThunderSTORM with Visualization options set to Normalized Gaussian and Lateral Uncertainty = λ/2/N.A..
Convert TIRF signal to distance map using NanoHills from Github.
Eliminate multiple blinks from each F(ab) or scFv using the molecular cut-off in Molecular modeling prep work steps 8-9.
Identify clusters using the molecular cut-off from Molecular modeling prep work step 11.
Identify pairs using the molecular cut-off from Molecular modeling prep work step 17.
Calculate the distance distributions for each of the conformations using Imaris Plugin software.
Compare measured distributions to Random, Face-to-face, Parallel, and Back-to-back configurations.
